metadata.case_name: CHAN KWUN TAK v. KWOK CHUN FONG

plaintiff.occupation_before: roast meat worker or supervisor of roast meat
plaintiff.occupation_after: he had taken on work in a kitchen but because of the residual disability resulting from the accident, he broke plates, fell down and even bumbed into a customer. Not surprisingly, after two days at this job he was sacked.

injuries.description: Severe injury to the head / cerebral injury (subarachnoid haemorrhage)
source: Because of the accident, the plaintiff had suffered severe injuries to his head and cervical spine, as a result of which the plaintiff suffers from neurological, orthopedic and psychiatric disabilities.
CT scan showed a subarachnoid haemorrhage.
Dr Kan... came to the conclusion that the plaintiff sustained injuries both to his brain and to his cervical spine as a result of the accident.

Doctor Kan assessed the severity of the cerebral injury to be of the most severe type based on the length of time of the plaintiff's continuous loss of memory and opined that it is inevitable that serious psychosomatic sequel would result from such injury.
After examining the plaintiff, he concluded that the plaintiff's sexual impairments are related to his head injury suffered at the accident.

injuries.description: Sprain to the neck / injury to the cervical spine
source: An MRI was performed and showed that the plaintiff suffered from cervical spondylosis. This resulted from a sprain to the plaintiff's neck from the accident.
Dr Kan... came to the conclusion that the plaintiff sustained injuries both to his brain and to his cervical spine as a result of the accident.
Doctor Tsoi... came to the conclusion that the plaintiff suffered from a head and neck injury during the accident but that his report deals only with the neck injury.

Doctor Tsoi commented that it is difficult to differentiate whether the plaintiff's neurological impairments affecting his limbs relates to his head or his neck injury, but that he can only estimate that half of the symptoms relating to the plaintiff's limbs were attributed to the neck injury.
injuries.icd_description: Acute whiplash associated disorder with complaint of neck pain with neurological signs

source: An MRI was performed and showed that the plaintiff suffered from cervical spondylosis. This resulted from a sprain to the plaintiff's neck from the accident.

X-ray revealed moderate degree of multiple levels of degenerative changes over the cervical spine, and this led him to the opinion that the cervical spondylosis was pre-existing and degenerative in nature.
the plaintiff was mentally normal before the accident but is now suffering from two mental disorders being a post-concussional disorder and a post-traumatic stress disorder.

As for the post-concussional disorder, Dr Chung puts this down as a result of the significant cerebral concussion sustained by the plaintiff during the accident, and which manifested itself with symptoms of difficulty in attention, poor memory, headaches, dizziness, irritability and depression.
Doctor Chung opines that this disorder is directly caused by the head trauma and it is likely that this disorder would be permanent and that further improvement of the symptoms will be slight.
the plaintiff was mentally normal before the accident but is now suffering from two mental disorders being a post-concussional disorder and a post-traumatic stress disorder.
As for the post-traumatic stress disorder, this manifests itself in a form of fear of cars and bad dreams related to the traffic accident.

The symptoms are directly caused by the trauma of the injury and the resultant problems which Dr Chung opines will often improve with time and these symptoms will gradually get better but will not subside completely. Doctor Chung further states that they will continue for some years to come.

manifestations.description: Numbness and pain of the upper and lower limbs as well as stiffness of the neck and shoulder.
Flexion of his head and neck would sent a lightening sensation down his limbs.
The pain and numbness in his lower limb gives him an unsteady and clumsy gait and makes him unable to squat without support.
He still suffers gripping or throbbing headaches frequently which are induced by neck movement.
He no longer suffers from attacks of vertigo, giddiness or near blackouts as before but now has a slight feeling of light-headedness at times.
He used to suffer from a mild degree of slurring in speech which has now improved, but he still finds it difficult to speak efficiently.
He has become absent-minded and forgetful and has poor concentration. His intelligence is affected in that his thoughts are muddled and is slow to react.
His sleeping pattern has improved now but he still becomes tired easily and feels exhausted physically and mentally. He feels a lack of stamina in general.
He is still irritable and short tempered and is depressed about his injury and his future.
He has become fearful of traffic and feels very tensed whenever he crosses the road.

treatments_received: admitted to Queen Elizabeth Hospital in an unconscious state
CT scan showed a subarachnoid haemorrhage and he was treated conservatively
transferred to Kowloon Hospital for rehabilitation on 14 July 1997
continued to receive out-patient rehabilitative treatment
received 79 sessions of occupational therapy at Kowloon Hospital
prescribed treatments to strengthen his limbs, to train his bilateral hand dexterity and to train his cognitive functions
psychological treatments for his cognitive impairments
psychological counselling for his temper outburst and anxiety
